To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dietary CLA increased hepatic CAT activity in the liver of growing broiler chickens.

dietary CLA at levels of 0.75%, 1.5%, and 2% did not affect antioxidant enzyme activities and lipid peroxidation in small intestine and liver tissues of broiler chickens fed a corn-based diet from 3 to 5 wk. However

dietary CLA did not affect the activities of antioxidant enzymes and the level of lipid peroxidative product, MDA, in the small intestinal mucosa and liver, except for hepatic CAT activity and lipid content.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of dietary conjugated lin oleic acid (CLA), a naturally occurring isomer of linoleic acid, on the antioxidant enzyme activities and lipid peroxidation in the intestinal mucosae and liver from broilers.
the effect of CLA on intestinal and hepatic antioxidant defense system and lipid peroxidation in broiler chickens.

the effect of dietary conjugated linolenic acid (CLA), on antioxidant enzymes including super oxide dismutase (SO), glutathione reductase peroxidase (GPX), catalase (CA) and glutathione-S-transferase (GST), as well as malondialdehyde level, a marker of lipid oxidation, in the small intestinal mucosa and liver from broilers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary CLA does not affect the antioxidant enzyme activity in small intestine or liver, and does not alter lipid peroxidation in these tissues of broiler chickens.
the dietary CLA has a negligible effect on intestinal and hepatic antioxidant enzyme activity, and lipid peroxidation in broiler chickens.
CLA has no effect on the intestinal antioxidant enzymes and the lipid peroxidation in the small intestine of broiler chickens.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CLA may have an effect on antioxidant defense system in the liver of the broiler chickens, but not in the intestine.
the dietary CLA could affect lipid metabolism, but not the antioxidant defense system in the liver of growing broiler chickens.
CLA may not be a potent antioxidant in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the antioxidant enzymes and lipid peroxidation in the small intestine are not affected by dietary CLA supplementation, but the antioxidant enzymes and peroxidation in liver tissues are influenced by dietary CLAs.
CLA can be used in broilers as a source of energy, and it has a beneficial effect on lipid metabolism in the broiler chickens.
CLA can be used in broiler diets to improve antioxidant status in liver and to reduce the risk of lipid peroxidative damage.
